html_bullets.point: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) partnered with Mongolia's Khan Bank to modernize its core digital banking platform using TCS BaNCS™, aiming to enhance customer experience for its 2.9 million customers and improve operational efficiencies.
TCS signed a digital transformation agreement with Dhofar Insurance Company to modernize its core insurance platform, enhancing customer and advisor experiences across various insurance offerings.
TCS partnered with Dhofar Insurance Company to implement TCS BaNCS™ for Insurance, enhancing customer experience and business agility.
TCS leased approximately 630,000 sq.ft. of office space in Chennai's Ozone Techno Park for a monthly rent of 2.8 crore, with a lease term of 10 years and a rent escalation of 12% every three years.
TCS leased a commercial building in Hyderabad for a monthly rent of Rs 4.37 crore, with a lease tenure of 15 years and a rent escalation of 12% every three years.

TCS launched AI-powered offerings including TCS SovereignSecure Cloud, TCS DigiBolt, and TCS Cyber Defense Suite, aimed at enhancing public sector growth and aligning with India's data localization requirements.

TCS sees significant growth opportunities in India's public sector, with a projected revenue increase of 62.6% year-on-year in constant currency terms, contributing 8.6% to its overall revenue of $30.18 billion for FY25.

TCS deferred annual wage hikes for its 607,000 employees due to business uncertainties, although it paid out 100% of the Quarterly Variable Allowance to over 70% of its workforce for the January-March quarter.
TCS hired 42,000 freshers in FY25, exceeding its target, and plans to continue this trend in FY26. However, the company delayed its wage hike cycle due to macroeconomic uncertainties.
TCS decided to defer wage hikes this year, contrasting with Infosys's proactive approach to wage increases.
TCS reported a 1.26% decline in net profit to Rs 12,224 crore in Q4 March 2025, while revenue from operations increased by 0.79% to Rs 64,479 crore compared to Q3 December 2024.
TCS grew its revenue by 3.78% in the last fiscal year, lagging behind mid-cap competitors.
TCS shares underperformed compared to other Tata Group companies from 2020 to 2024, as highlighted by Chairman N. Chandrasekaran.
TCS is experiencing a negative impact on growth expectations due to increased tariffs on Indian exports to the US, raising concerns about demand recovery in FY26.

TCS benefits from the India-UK Free Trade Agreement, which eases IT worker mobility and includes a three-year exemption on social security contributions for Indian professionals. The UK contributes 17% of TCS's overall revenue.
TCS issued reminder letters to shareholders regarding unclaimed dividends from the First Interim Dividend of 2018-19, notifying them of potential share transfers to the IEPF Authority.
